'''Soto ayam''' is a traditional [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian dish]] with ingredients such as chicken, ''[[lontong]]'', [[noodles]], and [[rice vermicelli]]. Soto ayam is also popular in [[Singapore]],<ref name="FlavoursofSingapore">{{cite web |url=http://www.flavoursofsingapore.nl/recipe-soto-ayam.htm | title= Singapore Chicken Soto Soup (Singapore Soto Ayam)}}</ref> [[Malaysia]]<ref name=Detik-Malaysia>{{cite news | url=http://news.detik.com/berita/3083497/ini-haji-paijan-orang-indonesia-yang-populerkan-soto-ayam-di-malaysia | title=Ini Haji Paijan, Orang Indonesia yang Populerkan Soto Ayam di Malaysia (This is Haji Paijian, the Indonesian who Popularised Soto Ayam in Malaysia) | work=DetikNews | date=30 November 2015 | access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref> and [[Suriname]], where it is made with slightly different ingredients and known as saoto. [[Turmeric]] is added as one of its main ingredients which makes the yellow chicken broth. It is one of the most popular variants of ''[[Soto (food)|soto]]'', a traditional soup commonly found in [[Indonesian cuisine]]. Besides chicken and vermicelli, it can also be served with hard-boiled [[egg (food)|eggs]], slices of fried potatoes, and [[Leaf celery|Chinese celery]] leaves. Fried [[shallot]]s are usually added as a [[garnish (food)|garnish]]. [[Coconut milk]] (''santan'') is also used as an additional ingredient.<ref name="Kruger 2014 p. 162"/> ''Koya'', a powder of mixed prawn crackers with fried garlic, or [[sambal]] is a common topping. ''[[Krupuk]]'' or ''[[emping]]'' is also a common topping. [[Lalab|Lalapan]] is usually served as a side dish.<ref name="soto ayam">{{cite web |url=http://www.resepsotoayam.com/ |title=Soto Ayam |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161026185624/http://www.resepsotoayam.com/ |archive-date=2016-10-26 }}</ref>
